A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic simulations, real-data benchmark experiments, a semi-synthetic NSLM evaluation and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds empirical assumption diagnostics, noisy privileged-information experiments and real-data TriplyRobust results.

M1.justification: The PCP, UI and TriplyRobust procedures remain unchanged. Section 3.2 explicitly restricts reference errors to uncorrupted samples, consistent with the residual distribution already specified in v1's proof of Theorem 4.

E1.justification: The original synthetic, tabular and NSLM datasets and tasks are retained. Appendix F.5 adds a weakened-information scenario by perturbing privileged information with Gaussian noise on Bio, Facebook1 and House.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Naive CP, Naive Imputation and applicable WCP/PCP comparators. Figure 16 adds results for the existing TriplyRobust method's estimated- and oracle-weight configurations.

E3.justification: Existing splits, preprocessing, models and training budgets remain unchanged. Appendix F.5 introduces test-set MSE and partial-correlation diagnostics conditional on privileged information, using observable proxies for theoretical quantities, plus a Gaussian-noise sweep.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained weight-error and imputation ablations, Appendix F.5 adds two substantive investigations: dependence diagnostics for Theorem 4's assumptions and sensitivity to weakened privileged information. These substantially expand scrutiny of UI's validity conditions and robustness.

E5.justification: New analyses report 10 random splits for Table 4 and four for Figure 15. Table 4 introduces plus/minus summaries, without identifying the uncertainty quantity. Existing repeated-run reporting is retained; the new counts do not establish increased replication of earlier experiments.

E6.justification: Figures 1–14 retain their results. Substantial additions include Table 4's dependence, MSE and coverage results, Figure 15's noisy-PI trends, and Figure 16's TriplyRobust coverage and interval lengths on five benchmarks. Table 4 reports UI coverage of 90.72%, 90.96% and 91.23% on Bio, Facebook1 and House, respectively.

T1.justification: Localized corrections align retained statements with their explanations: Theorem 3 and Propositions 3–4 reverse the comparisons accompanying XOR/NXOR, while Theorem 4 and Lemma 3 reverse both density inequalities from >= to <=. Appendix A.1.2 also corrects weight normalization. The theorem inventory and proof structures remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions remain robustness analysis for inaccurate weights, uncertainty-preserving imputation, and a triply robust union valid when an underlying method's assumptions hold. Added emphasis and evidence do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 explains that residual independence need not require small estimation errors. Appendix F.5 interprets its proxy diagnostics and noisy-PI results as evidence of robustness beyond exact assumptions, while F.6 discusses how inaccurate weights affect ensemble interval widths.

D1.justification: Appendix E.3 newly states that experiments typically take at most 10 minutes. Section 3.2 makes the clean-reference-sample restriction explicit. The documented hyperparameters, hardware, data-generation procedures and code access otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New references and examples broaden practical privileged-information context, including Ortiz-Jimenez et al. (2023), Lopez-Paz et al. (2015) and Yang et al. (2022). Javanmardi et al. (2024) supports a new future-work connection. The central positioning relative to PCP and worst-case weight-error analyses is retained.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the introduction, assumption explanations and experiments. The existing Theorem 5 proof receives an A.3 heading, and F.5–F.6 are appended. Main section organization remains stable; citation style, front matter and acknowledgments change.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 4 and Figures 15–16 while retaining the original fourteen figure contents. The ICLR template changes the title, author block and headers; algorithms and tables reflow, Table 1 becomes taller, and several captions are shortened.

improvement.justification: Corrected mathematical inequalities reduce internal inconsistencies, and clearer assumptions plus new diagnostics improve assessability. Figure 16 also documents ensemble performance beyond v1's synthetic demonstration. These are useful, limited gains: the dependence checks substitute proxies for theoretical quantities, and the noisy-PI study uses only four splits.
